faqs.question: Why are there 0 vacancies in Bihar, Jharkhand, Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand, etc. in SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: Because the 1,538 vacancies in this particular notification are backlog vacancies, not the new regular vacancies for the 2026–27 recruitment cycle. A backlog vacancy generally represents a reserved-category vacancy from an earlier recruitment that remained unfilled. Therefore, the distribution is completely different from what you would expect from a normal SBI Clerk notification. Zero in Delhi/Bihar/Haryana etc. does NOT mean SBI will have zero regular Clerk vacancies there this year.

faqs.question: Will SBI Clerk 2026 vacancies be updated or increased later?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but don't assume they will be. The current notification is specifically for the backlog drive. The much more important development for most aspirants will be the separate regular SBI Clerk notification, which should contain fresh state-wise vacancies for the new recruitment cycle. If your state has zero seats in the present notification, wait for the regular notification rather than concluding that SBI Clerk has no vacancy in your state.

faqs.question: Why is there no vacancy in Delhi, Haryana, and NCR for SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: This is a consequence of the backlog-vacancy nature of the current recruitment. It does not mean SBI has stopped recruiting Junior Associates in Delhi/NCR or Haryana. Also remember that SBI recruitment is organized according to State/UT/circle-wise vacancies, rather than simply according to where candidates live.

faqs.question: What should candidates from zero-vacancy states do for SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: Wait for the regular notification. If you're from Delhi, Haryana, Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab, Uttarakhand, etc., choosing another state merely because it has backlog vacancies is not recommended unless you genuinely satisfy that state's local-language requirement and are eligible for the applicable reserved category. The regular notification is likely to be far more relevant.

faqs.question: Can I apply for SBI Clerk 2026 from another state?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to the notification's conditions — but the important issue is the local language. SBI's Junior Associate recruitment is state/UT based. Candidates apply for vacancies of one State/UT only and must qualify the specified local-language test (LPT) where applicable. For example, living in Delhi does not prevent you from applying for Maharashtra, but if you select Maharashtra, you must be prepared for Marathi language requirements.

faqs.question: How strict is the Language Proficiency Test (LPT) in SBI Clerk recruitment?
faqs.answer: It is a mandatory qualifying requirement. The LPT checks whether you know the specified local language of the selected state (e.g., Marathi for Maharashtra, Gujarati for Gujarat, Tamil for Tamil Nadu, Odia for Odisha, Kannada for Karnataka, Malayalam for Kerala, Punjabi for Punjab, Bengali for West Bengal, Hindi/Urdu for UP). Candidates who cannot produce acceptable proof of having studied the specified local language in 10th or 12th standard must qualify the LPT. Failing the required LPT will result in disqualification.

faqs.question: Will applying outside your home state automatically cause LPT problems?
faqs.answer: No. Your home state is not the deciding factor. The important question is whether you can prove/meet the language requirement of the state applied for. A candidate from Delhi could apply for Maharashtra, but if they cannot establish Marathi proficiency through standard qualification routes, they may have to take the LPT. Do not choose a state simply because it has a lower cutoff.

faqs.question: If I apply for SBI Clerk from another state, where will my exam centre be?
faqs.answer: You can generally appear for the Preliminary and Mains examination at a notified examination centre of your choice/availability, subject to SBI's arrangements. However, your recruitment is against the state applied for. SBI's rules state that the local-language test (LPT) is conducted at a centre decided by SBI in the state applied for, at the candidate's own expense. (Exam centre ≠ state of recruitment).

faqs.question: How should candidates choose a state when applying for SBI Clerk?
faqs.answer: Choose the state where you genuinely satisfy the local-language requirement first; then compare vacancies and expected competition. The recommended sequence is: Language eligibility → vacancy → expected competition → posting preference. Remember that candidates are considered against the State/UT applied for and are posted in that state if selected.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Regular and Backlog vacancies in SBI recruitment?
faqs.answer: A Regular vacancy is a newly identified vacancy for the current recruitment cycle. A Backlog vacancy is a reserved vacancy from an earlier recruitment that remained unfilled and is carried forward to be filled through a special drive. The current 1,538-post notification is specifically a backlog recruitment, which explains the unusual state-wise vacancy distribution.

faqs.question: Can eligible candidates apply for both Regular and Backlog SBI Clerk recruitments?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you are eligible for both and SBI permits applications for both drives. They are separate recruitment drives. For example, an eligible SC/ST/OBC candidate could potentially participate in both the backlog recruitment and the upcoming regular recruitment, provided they satisfy the eligibility conditions of both.

faqs.question: Will the exams for SBI Clerk Regular and Backlog recruitments be separate?
faqs.answer: Do not assume they will be combined. The current notification is a separate Special Recruitment Drive, so candidates should treat it as a separate recruitment unless SBI subsequently announces otherwise. Expect separate application and exam processes.

faqs.question: Can General (Unreserved) candidates apply for these SBI Clerk backlog vacancies?
faqs.answer: No. The 1,538 backlog vacancies are reserved exclusively for SC, ST, and OBC candidates carried forward from previous recruitment drives. Unreserved / General category candidates cannot claim an SC/ST/OBC backlog seat.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and cutoff date for SBI Clerk Special Drive 2026?
faqs.answer: For the backlog notification, the basic age requirement is 20 to 28 years as of the cut-off date specified in the official notification, plus applicable relaxations for reserved categories (5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, up to 10–15 years for PwBD). Ensure you check your exact Date of Birth against the specific cut-off date stated in the notification.

faqs.question: Why are some states showing SC/ST vacancies but zero OBC vacancies?
faqs.answer: Because backlog vacancies are category-specific. If SBI had an SC/ST backlog in a particular state but no OBC backlog, it cannot convert or reassign those seats. A table showing SC: 0 | ST: 12 | OBC: 0 simply reflects historical unfilled reserved positions for that state, not a policy of ignoring OBC candidates.

faqs.question: Is the SBI Clerk 2026 question paper available in English?
faqs.answer: Yes. The examination paper is provided in English along with Hindi and the relevant regional language(s) depending on the state (e.g., English/Hindi/Marathi in Maharashtra, English/Hindi/Gujarati in Gujarat, English/Hindi/Odia in Odisha, English/Hindi/Bengali in WB, English/Hindi/Urdu in UP/Bihar). The question paper medium is separate from the LPT requirement.

faqs.question: Did SBI Apprentice recruitment reduce regular Clerk vacancies?
faqs.answer: No. There is no basis in the official notification to conclude that Apprentice recruitment reduced Clerk vacancies. SBI Apprentice and SBI Junior Associate are different recruitment streams. The 1,538-post announcement is a backlog drive, and the upcoming regular Junior Associate recruitment will provide the actual fresh vacancy numbers.

faqs.question: Why are videos claiming 9,000 to 11,000+ vacancies when this notification says 1,538?
faqs.answer: Because numbers like 9,000 or 11,000+ circulating online represent projected estimates for the upcoming Regular recruitment cycle, whereas 1,538 is the officially notified count for the Special Backlog Drive. Do not add backlog figures to unofficial YouTube estimates; wait for SBI's official regular notification.

faqs.question: Where can candidates download the official SBI Clerk notification PDF?
faqs.answer: The official notification should always be downloaded directly from SBI's official careers portal at sbi.bank.in/web/careers or bank.sbi/careers. Always verify the advertisement on SBI's official site rather than relying on unverified Telegram or social media files.

faqs.question: Should students run a Twitter/X campaign regarding uneven SBI Clerk vacancies?
faqs.answer: Campaigns will not force SBI to convert reserved backlog seats into UR seats, as backlog vacancies are legally reserved carried-forward positions. If raising concerns, the appropriate request to SBI would be to clarify state-wise vacancy requirements and release the regular SBI Clerk notification with fresh vacancies at the earliest.

overview: Himachal Pradesh Public Service Commission (HPPSC) and HP Police Department have jointly released two concurrent recruitment notifications on 10 July 2026 for the post of Constable (IRB/District Police). Advertisement No. 57/7-2026 covers 491 Male Constable posts and Advertisement No. 58/7-2026 covers 243 Female Constable posts — a combined total of 734 constable vacancies across Himachal Pradesh.

Candidates must apply separately under the respective advertisement number via the Himachal Pradesh Online Recruitment Application (HP ORA) portal. A single application fee of ₹600/- applies for all candidates irrespective of category. Last date for online application for both advertisements is 31 August 2026 (11:59 PM).

Selection is conducted in four stages: Physical Standard Test (PST), Physical Efficiency Test (PET), Written Examination (90 MCQs), and NCC Certificate Evaluation. Final merit list is out of 100 marks: Written Exam (90 Marks) + Height marks (6 Marks) + NCC marks (4 Marks).

overview: The Indian Air Force (IAF) has released the Official Notification for Open Recruitment Rally for enrolment of unmarried Indian male and female candidates as Agniveervayu (Other Than Science Subjects) for Intake 01/2027.
The Open Recruitment Rally will be held from 31st August 2026 to 07th September 2026 at two designated rally venues in Nagaland (Chumoukedima) and Andaman & Nicobar Islands (Port Blair).

Target States & Union Territories: 1) Chumoukedima (Nagaland) venue covers all districts of Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura, and Sikkim; 2) Sri Vijaya Puram (Port Blair) venue covers all districts of UT of Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

Rally Schedule at Nagaland (NAPTC Chumoukedima): Women Candidates: 01-02 Sept 2026 (Reporting 01 Sept); Men Candidates: 04-05 Sept 2026 (Reporting 04 Sept). Cut-off reporting time is 10:00 AM on reporting date.

Rally Schedule at Andaman & Nicobar (Netaji Stadium, Port Blair): Women Candidates: 01-02 Sept 2026 (Reporting 01 Sept); Men Candidates: 03-04 Sept 2026 (Reporting 03 Sept). Cut-off reporting time is 10:00 AM on reporting date.

Date of Birth Block: Candidates born between 01 January 2005 and 01 July 2009 (both dates inclusive) are eligible to appear in the Open Recruitment Rally. Upper age limit on date of enrolment is 22 years.

Educational Qualification: Passed 10+2 / Intermediate / Equivalent Examination in any stream from recognized Central/State Education Board with minimum 50% aggregate marks and 50% marks in English; OR Passed 2-year Vocational Course with 50% aggregate and 50% English; OR Passed 3-year Diploma Course in Engineering (Mechanical/Electrical/Electronics/Auto/CSE/IT/Instrumentation) with 50% aggregate and 50% English.

Monthly Stipend & Agniveer Package: 1st Year: ₹30,000/- (In-Hand ₹21,000); 2nd Year: ₹33,000/- (In-Hand ₹23,100); 3rd Year: ₹36,500/- (In-Hand ₹25,550); 4th Year: ₹40,000/- (In-Hand ₹28,000). Total Agniveer Corpus Fund contribution after 4 years is ₹5.02 Lakhs.

Seva Nidhi Package on Exit: One-time Seva Nidhi Package of approximately ₹10.04 Lakhs (candidate's contribution + matching Govt contribution + interest) on completion of 4 years engagement. Up to 25% of each batch will be enrolled in regular cadre of Indian Air Force as Airman.

Selection Process: 1) Initial Certificate Verification -> 2) Physical Fitness Test (PFT-I & PFT-II) -> 3) Objective Written Test (45 mins: English 20 Qs + RAGA 30 Qs) -> 4) Adaptability Test-I -> 5) Adaptability Test-II -> 6) Medical Examination (at 11 ASC Jorhat / 8 ASC Sri Vijaya Puram in Sept 2026).

overview: Directorate of Education Recruitment (Sikhiya Bharti Directorate), Punjab (Sector-60, S.A.S. Nagar, Mohali) has published official public recruitment notice Ref No. ਈ-888608/2026208471 dated 31-07-2026 for filling 2000 fresh vacancies of Physical Training Instructor (PTI) (Primary Cadre).

The recruitment is governed by the Punjab State Elementary Education (Physical Training Instructor) Service Rules, 2023 and Punjab State Elementary Education (Physical Training Instructor) Service (First Amendment) Rules, 2025.

Total Fresh Vacancies: 2000 Posts — General: 780, EWS: 200, SC (M&B): 200, SC (R&O): 200, BC: 200, Ex-Servicemen: 260, Sports Quota: 60, Physically Handicapped: 80, Freedom Fighter: 20. Out of total vacancies, 650 posts are horizontally reserved for women across all categories.

Educational Qualification: Passed 10+2 (Higher Secondary/Senior Secondary) with at least 2 years Diploma or Certificate in Physical Education (D.P.Ed / C.P.Ed) or equivalent recognized course. Candidates appearing in final year of D.P.Ed/C.P.Ed can apply provided they obtain and produce the diploma before the final written recruitment examination date.

Mandatory Language Criteria: Passed Matriculation (10th) with Punjabi as a compulsory or elective subject. Additionally, candidates must clear a mandatory Punjabi Language Qualifying Test (10th standard level) with at least 50% marks as per G.S.R.72/Const./Art.309/Amd.(22)/2022 dated 28/10/2022.
Selection Method (Total 100 Marks): Written Objective Test on Subject (70 Marks) + Sports Achievement Gradation Weightage (Max 30 Marks) + Mandatory Qualifying Physical Eligibility Test (PET).

Physical Eligibility Test (PET): Qualifying test consisting of 5 events (30m flying start, standing broad jump, 6x10m shuttle run, bend and reach, 1600m run). Candidate must successfully complete at least 3 out of 5 components to qualify. PwD candidates are exempt from PET.

Pay Scale & Emoluments: Fixed Initial Pay of Rs. 29,200/- per month without any allowance during 3 years probation period as per Punjab State Elementary Education (Physical Training Instructor) Rules 2023 & Amendment 2025.

Application Fee: Rs. 2000/- for General & Other Unreserved Categories; Rs. 1000/- for Reserved Categories (SC / ST / BC of Punjab State). Ex-Servicemen (Self) are completely exempted from application fee.
How to Apply: Online application portal erd.punjab.gov.in will remain open from 01 August 2026 to 31 August 2026.

overview: SJVN Limited, a Navratna CPSE under the administrative control of Ministry of Power, Government of India, was incorporated on May 24, 1988 as a Joint Venture of Government of India (GOI) and Government of Himachal Pradesh (GOHP).

SJVN invites applications from experienced professionals having expertise in Erection / Commissioning & O&M of Thermal Power Plants for its fully owned subsidiary SJVN Thermal Private Limited (STPL), executing the 1320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project in Bihar.

A total of 21 executive positions are advertised across Mechanical, Electrical, Control & Instrumentation (C&I), and Chemical disciplines at Chief General Manager / E8(a), Deputy Manager / E4, and Engineer / E2 levels.
Selected candidates will be placed in attractive IDA pay scales ranging from ₹50,000 - ₹2,80,000 along with Cafeteria benefits, HRA, PRP, Provident Fund, Medical, and Gratuity as per CPSE rules.

Deputy Manager / E4 Executive Experience: Min 7 years post-qualification executive experience in Erection/Commissioning and/or O&M of Coal based Thermal Power Plant, out of which at least 3 years relevant O&M experience in Super Critical Thermal Power Plant of min 660 MW capacity.

selectionProcess.description: Applications will be scrutinized on the basis of essential qualification, relevant thermal power plant experience, pay scale / CTC criteria.
If the number of applicants is large, SJVN may conduct a qualifying screening test (50% qualifying marks for UR/EWS/ESM and 40% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD) to restrict candidates called for interview.
Final selection will be done purely based on marks secured in the Personal Interview. Qualifying marks in interview are 50% for UR/EWS/ESM and 40% for reserved categories.
Selected candidates will undergo original document verification and medical examination as per SJVN medical rules.

howToApply: Step 1: Visit the official website of SJVN Limited at www.sjvn.nic.in and navigate to the Career section.
Step 2: Click on "Advt. No. 127/2026 - Executive Recruitment for STPL Buxar Thermal Power Project".
Step 3: Register using a valid E-mail ID and Mobile Number.
Step 4: Fill in personal details, educational qualifications, and chronological executive experience in thermal power plants.
Step 5: Upload recent passport size color photograph with white background (max 50 KB) and signature in blue/black ink (max 50 KB).
Step 6: Pay the online non-refundable application fee of ₹500 + 18% GST (if applicable).
Step 7: Submit the online application form and take a printout of the Application Form preview.

Step 8: Send the self-attested hard copy of the Application Form along with payment receipt, qualification certificates, experience letters, pay slips / Form 16 / ITR, and turnover certificates by post to: O/o DGM (HR/Recruitment) SJVN Limited, Shakti Sadan, Corporate Head Quarters, Shanan Shimla, HP-171006 before 15/09/2026.
documentsRequired: Printout of Online Application Form & Fee Payment Receipt.
10th / Matriculation Certificate as proof of Date of Birth.
Engineering Degree / M.Sc Degree Certificates & Semester Marksheets showing minimum 55% / 50% aggregate marks.
Chronological Work Experience Certificates, Appointment Letters, Offer Letters, Promotion Orders, Service Certificates, Relieving Letters.
Pay Slips & PF Slips for the last 6 months for relevant pay scale proof.
For Private Sector Candidates: Form 16 & ITR of last 2 Financial Years, Last Pay Certificate stating CTC, and Audited Company Turnover Proof (min ₹2500 Cr annual turnover).
Valid Caste / Category Certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL/EWS/PwBD, if applicable).
importantInstructions: Experience in Super Critical Thermal Power Plants of minimum 660 MW capacity is MANDATORY as specified per post.
Private sector candidates must produce proof of working in an organization with an average annual turnover of at least ₹2,500 Crore in the last 3 financial years.
Teaching, Internship, Apprenticeship, or Pre-qualification experience will NOT be counted towards executive experience.
Hard copy application along with required certificates must reach the SJVN Shimla office on or before 15.09.2026.
For any recruitment queries, email: recruitment@sjvn.nic.in with "Advt. No. 127/2026 and Designation" in the subject line.

faqs.question: Where can I get the 1-year experience certificate?
faqs.answer: The 1-year sanitation work experience certificate must be issued by a competent authority as specified in the official recruitment notification. The experience should clearly show that you have worked in cleaning/sanitation-related duties for at least one year. Before applying, ensure your certificate matches the prescribed format and issuing authority mentioned in the notification. Submitting an invalid certificate may lead to rejection of your application.

faqs.question: Is a contractor (Thekedar) experience certificate valid?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether the contractor and the experience certificate satisfy the conditions laid down in the official notification. A certificate issued by a private contractor is not automatically valid. Candidates should carefully verify that the issuing authority and the certificate format are accepted by the recruitment rules before applying.

faqs.question: Is sanitation work experience from a government hospital valid?
faqs.answer: If you worked in sanitation or cleaning duties in a government hospital and your experience certificate has been issued by the competent authority in accordance with the recruitment rules, it may be considered valid. The final decision will be taken by the recruiting authority during document verification.

faqs.question: Is experience from a hotel, private office, or private company accepted?
faqs.answer: Experience from a hotel, private office, or private company may be accepted only if it fulfills all the eligibility conditions mentioned in the official notification and is supported by a valid experience certificate issued by the competent authority. Candidates should not assume that every private-sector certificate will be accepted.

faqs.question: Can an NCC or NSS certificate be used instead of the experience certificate?
faqs.answer: No. NCC, NSS, Scout, or similar certificates cannot replace the mandatory 1-year sanitation work experience certificate. These certificates may reflect extracurricular participation but do not count as professional sanitation work experience unless specifically stated in the official notification.

faqs.question: Will selection be through a lottery or a written exam?
faqs.answer: As per the official notification, there is no written examination for this recruitment. The selection process will be carried out according to the procedure prescribed by the Rajasthan Government. Candidates should rely only on the official notification and avoid rumours circulating on social media regarding the selection process.

faqs.question: Is the selection based on money or corruption?
faqs.answer: No candidate should believe or pay money to anyone claiming to guarantee selection. The recruitment process is conducted by the competent government authority. If anyone demands money in exchange for selection, candidates should immediately report the matter to the concerned authorities. Trust only official notifications and announcements.

faqs.question: Should there be a written examination?
faqs.answer: Many candidates believe that a written examination would make the recruitment process more transparent. However, the recruitment process is decided by the Rajasthan Government. Candidates must follow the selection method prescribed in the official notification.

faqs.question: Is the salary only ₹7,000?
faqs.answer: No. The amount of ₹7,000 generally refers to the fixed remuneration during the probation/training period, if applicable. After successful completion of the probation period, employees receive salary according to the applicable Pay Matrix and government rules, along with admissible allowances. Candidates should refer to the official notification for exact salary details.

faqs.question: Will Safai Karamcharis have to clean drains and perform sanitation work?
faqs.answer: Yes. The duties of a Safai Karamchari generally include sanitation work such as cleaning roads, public places, drains, waste collection, and maintaining cleanliness as assigned by the local body. The exact responsibilities depend on the department and place of posting.

faqs.question: Can PWD (Persons with Disabilities) candidates apply?
faqs.answer: PWD candidates can apply if vacancies are reserved for their disability category and they satisfy all the eligibility conditions mentioned in the notification. Candidates should carefully check the reservation details and the list of eligible benchmark disabilities before submitting their application.

faqs.question: Who is eligible to apply?
faqs.answer: Candidates who satisfy the prescribed age limit, required sanitation work experience, and other eligibility conditions mentioned in the official notification can apply. All applicants must also fulfill the document and category requirements specified by the recruiting authority.

faqs.question: Can candidates from other states apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates from other states can generally apply if they fulfill the eligibility conditions. However, they may not receive the benefit of reservation available to Rajasthan domicile candidates unless specifically provided in the notification.

faqs.question: When will the Rajasthan Forest Guard Recruitment be released?
faqs.answer: The Rajasthan Government has not yet officially announced the next Forest Guard recruitment. Candidates should regularly check the Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB/RSMSSB) website and trusted job portals for the latest updates.

faqs.question: When will the Rajasthan Jal Vibhag ITI Recruitment be released?
faqs.answer: As of now, no official notification has been released for the Rajasthan Jal Vibhag ITI recruitment. Once the notification is published, details regarding vacancies, eligibility, syllabus, and the application process will be available on the official website.

faqs.question: What is the syllabus for Rajasthan Jal Vibhag ITI Recruitment?
faqs.answer: The syllabus will be released only after the official notification is published. Generally, ITI recruitments include questions related to the candidate's trade, General Knowledge, Reasoning, Mathematics, and basic language skills, depending on the specific post. Candidates should wait for the official syllabus before starting focused preparation.

overview: IIFCL Projects Limited (IPL), a prestigious wholly-owned subsidiary of India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) - a 100% Government of India Enterprise, has officially announced a rolling advertisement for the engagement of Individual Consultants (IC) on a full-time, contractual basis. With a mandate to deliver expert Financial & Infrastructure Advisory services to Central & State Governments, Local Bodies, and Private Developers across India, IPL is building a robust database of highly qualified professionals. This rolling recruitment campaign operates continuously throughout the year, allowing eligible candidates to submit their applications at any time to be considered for active project requirements in multiple sectors, including roads, highways, ports, power, water supply, renewable energy, tourism, and solid waste management.

This recruitment campaign offers a wide array of opportunities, spanning across 65 specialized consultant profiles. These encompass diverse areas such as Project & Contract Management, Procurement, Financial & Costing, IT & MIS, Digital Public Infrastructure, Legal Management, Corporate Communications, Tourism Development, Master Planning, PPP & Investment, and Environmental Affairs. The vacancies are not fixed to a static count, as hiring is on a rolling basis, meaning candidate requirements are fulfilled dynamically as mandates arise. The position grades range from Young Professionals to Senior Consultants (Grades I, II, and III) based on years of post-qualification experience. Selected professionals will be stationed at IPL's Head Office in New Delhi or branch offices and project sites across various States including Amaravati (AP), Chennai, Ahmedabad, the Northeast Region, and other locations on an "Anywhere in India" basis.

The eligibility criteria vary depending on the specific IC Code of interest. Educational requirements range from Graduate degrees in Engineering (B.E./B.Tech), Architecture, Planning, or Law (LLB/LLM) to Postgraduate degrees, MBA/PGDM, CA, CWA, or CFA from recognized premium national or international institutes. Remuneration is highly attractive and structured based on experience: Young Professionals receive a fixed pay of ₹70,000 per month; Grade I Consultants receive between ₹80,000 and ₹1,45,000; Grade II Consultants earn from ₹1,45,000 to ₹2,65,000; and Senior Consultants (Grade III) are eligible for ₹2,65,000 to ₹3,30,000 per month. The upper age limits are 32, 45, 50, and 62 years respectively.

Interested and qualified candidates can apply either by email or physical post. The application window is open for exactly one year from the date of publishing the advertisement, running on a rolling basis. Candidate selection is based entirely on an Interview process (either in Delhi or via online mode), which follows preliminary shortlisting of applicants matching the company's rigorous experience, suitability, and business criteria. There is no application fee for any category, making this a transparent, merit-based entry into one of India's leading government-backed infrastructure advisory firms.

faqs.question: What is the full form of IPL, and who is its parent organization?
faqs.answer: IPL stands for IIFCL Projects Limited, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL), a 100% Government of India Enterprise.

faqs.question: What is the main objective of IIFCL Projects Limited (IPL)?
faqs.answer: The main objective of IPL is to provide Financial & Infrastructure Advisory services to various Central & State Governments, their affiliates, Local Bodies, and Private Developers, along with Capacity Building and Policy Advocacy services.

faqs.question: What is the nature of the engagement for the Individual Consultants (IC) positions?
faqs.answer: The engagement of Individual Consultants is on a full-time, contractual basis. Selected candidates are not allowed to take up any other appointment, engagement, or assignment during their contract period.

faqs.question: Where will the selected Individual Consultants be stationed?
faqs.answer: Selected consultants are expected to be stationed at IPL's Head Office in Delhi, and/or any of its branch offices, and/or across various States wherein IPL is currently working or intends to work under mandate.

faqs.question: What does rolling recruitment mean for this IPL notification?
faqs.answer: It means that applications are accepted and evaluated throughout the year on an as-and-when needed basis. IPL maintains an active database of applications, and candidates are selected from this pool whenever vacancies arise in specific areas of work.

faqs.question: What is the duration of the rolling applications window?
faqs.answer: The applications window is open for exactly one year from the date of publishing the advertisement.

faqs.question: What are the four grades of Individual Consultants, and what is their required experience?
faqs.answer: The grades are: (1) Young Professional with 1 year experience; (2) Consultant Grade I with 3 - 8 years experience; (3) Consultant Grade II with 8 - 15 years experience; and (4) Senior Consultant with 15 years or more experience.

faqs.question: What is the monthly remuneration for a Young Professional?
faqs.answer: A Young Professional is paid a fixed monthly consolidated remuneration of ₹70,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly salary range for a Consultant Grade I?
faqs.answer: The monthly remuneration range for Consultant Grade I is ₹80,000 to ₹1,45,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly salary range for a Consultant Grade II?
faqs.answer: The monthly remuneration range for Consultant Grade II is ₹1,45,000 to ₹2,65,000.

faqs.question: What is the monthly salary range for a Senior Consultant (Grade III)?
faqs.answer: The monthly remuneration range for Senior Consultant (Grade III) is ₹2,65,000 to ₹3,30,000.

faqs.question: How is the final remuneration decided for selected candidates?
faqs.answer: The final remuneration within the corresponding grade band is decided based on the candidate's expectations, experience, and expertise. The decision of IPL is final and binding.

faqs.question: Is TA/DA provided for official tours during the engagement?
faqs.answer: Yes. Consultants are allowed to undertake official tours as required by their duties, and TA/DA and Hotel Accommodation are paid or reimbursed as per the company's policy.

faqs.question: What are the upper age limits for different grades of consultants?
faqs.answer: The upper age limits are: 32 years for Young Professional, 45 years for Consultant Grade I, 50 years for Consultant Grade II, and 62 years for Senior Consultant.

faqs.question: What are the essential academic qualifications required to apply?
faqs.answer: Qualifications depend on the specific IC Code but generally include regular Graduation/Post Graduation in Engineering (B.E./B.Tech/B.Arch/B.Plan/M.Tech/M.Plan), Master's/Postgraduate degrees, MBA, CA, CWA, CFA, LLB, or LLM from recognized premier institutes.

faqs.question: Are candidates with degrees from foreign universities eligible?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided they can produce an equivalency certificate issued by a Competent Authority certifying that their foreign qualification is treated at par with qualifications offered by Indian Institutes/Universities.

faqs.question: What is the selection procedure for these consultant posts?
faqs.answer: The selection is done through a Personal Interview after preliminary screening and shortlisting of applications based on qualifications, experience, suitability, city preference, and business requirements.

faqs.question: Where will the Personal Interviews be conducted, and is travel allowance provided?
faqs.answer: Shortlisted applicants will attend the interview in Delhi or online. No travel expense reimbursement (TA/DA) is paid for appearing in the interview.

faqs.question: What is the initial period of engagement for these contractual positions?
faqs.answer: Individual Consultants are engaged for an initial fixed period of two years.

faqs.question: Can the period of contract be extended, and what is the maximum limit?
faqs.answer: Yes, the contract can be extended by one year at a time up to a maximum tenure of 5 years (i.e. 2+1+1+1 years), contingent on a satisfactory Annual Performance Review based on KPIs.

faqs.question: How can candidates apply for this recruitment, and are there different email addresses?
faqs.answer: Candidates must apply by email or post. There are separate email addresses: recruitment1@iifclprojects.com for IC Codes 01 to 10; recruitment2@iifclprojects.com for IC Codes 13 to 46; and recruitment3@iifclprojects.com for IC Codes 11, 12, and 47 to 65.

faqs.question: What documents must be submitted along with the application?
faqs.answer: Submission requires: the filled application form in MS Word (Editable) and PDF formats (signed on each page), a signed Advertisement Notice, copies of educational certificates/marksheets, experience certificates, latest salary slips, and an equivalency certificate if applicable.

faqs.question: What is the subject line format required for sending the application by email?
faqs.answer: The Subject Line format must be: "Application_ IC CODE_ [Insert IC Code] _ [Name of Applicant]" (e.g. Application_ IC CODE_ 01 _ Rahul Sharma).

faqs.question: What is the physical postal address to submit applications?
faqs.answer: AGM- HR, IIFCL Projects Limited (IPL), 3rd Floor, Tower - E, World Trade Centre (WTC), Nauroji Nagar, New Delhi - 110029.

faqs.question: Can a candidate apply for more than one Individual Consultant post?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the applicant must apply separately for each IC Code and Grade Code.

faqs.question: What happens if a candidate provides incorrect or falsified documents?
faqs.answer: Their candidature will stand cancelled immediately at any stage of selection, and if detected after appointment, their services are liable to be terminated without any compensation.

syllabus: Post Code 01 (Bioinstrumentation / Biophysics / Medical Physics): Design & validation of wearable health monitoring sensors and systems & biomedical sensor instrumentation; bio-signal data acquisition & processing (ECG, EEG, EMG), noise reduction & feature extraction; medical imaging and informatics; development of portable diagnostic devices and wearable sensors.

Post Code 02 (Developmental Biology / Biotechnology): Radiation biology & exposure models; regenerative approaches to preserve musculoskeletal integrity during spaceflight; mammalian and stem cell culture, primary cell lines, 3D/organoid culture systems; in vivo and ex vivo animal physiological studies; astronaut disease biology models; host-pathogen interaction studies under stress and microgravity.

Post Code 03 (Cellular & Molecular Biology / Cell Biology): Immune and cellular adaptation across astronaut health cycle; bioinformatics analysis of proteomic data for biomarker identification; molecular cloning, confocal microscopy, live-cell imaging, gene editing; large-scale proteomic dataset analysis, gene expression & statistical workflows.

Post Code 04 (Computational Biology / Systems Biology / Bioinformatics): In-silico models to anticipate astronaut adaptation, assess countermeasures & guide rehabilitation; development of therapeutics and space-grade diagnostics; multi-omics integration for spaceflight stressors; modeling cellular pathways, host-microbe interactions & metabolic networks; computational simulation of closed-loop life support systems; generative models & Digital Twin Biology using neural networks and deep learning.

Post Code 05 (Biomedical Engineering / Biomechanics): Gait analysis, exercise countermeasure, motion capture & force-plate studies, rehabilitation program development; biomechanical analysis of musculoskeletal system; human performance data analysis from wearables; rodent/human analog design for spaceflight experiments.

Post Code 06 (Biomedical Engineering / Bio-imaging & DSP): Development & validation of bio-imaging systems for microgravity tissue changes (strictly confidential); implementation of DSP algorithms for ECG/EEG/EMG from wearables; bioinformatics dataset analysis for space radiation effects; portable diagnostic devices, biosensors, point-of-care testing & real-time astronaut health monitoring; biomedical device & lab-on-chip integration; AI/ML integration for real-time signal/imaging analysis.

overview: Chhattisgarh Staff Selection Board, Raipur (CGSSB / CG Vyapam) has released official notification F-20/2026/3399 inviting Online Applications for the Written Recruitment Examination for Teacher (Shikshak) posts under Directorate of Public Instruction, Government of Chhattisgarh under Exam Code LST26.

Candidates seeking recruitment in Chhattisgarh School Education Department can submit online profile registration and application form on cgssb.cgstate.gov.in or vyapamcg.cgstate.gov.in from 07 August 2026 to 02 September 2026 (5:00 PM).

As per Government of Chhattisgarh rules, application fee paid by local resident candidates of Chhattisgarh who appear in the examination will be 100% refunded directly into their bank accounts after the declaration of exam results.
The Written Competitive Exam (LST26) is tentatively scheduled for Sunday, 25 October 2026 (10:00 AM to 12:15 PM) across 16 District Headquarters in Chhattisgarh.

overview: High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL), Pune, a premier R&D establishment under Defence Research & Development Organization (DRDO), Ministry of Defence, Govt. of India, has released official advertisement HEMRL/HRD/APPRENTICE/2026-27/01 for engagement of Graduate Apprentices for One Year Apprentice Training (2026-27).

A total of 50 vacancies are available across various engineering and general degree streams: Chemical (10), Mechanical (8), Chemistry (9), Computer Science/IT (5), E&TC (3), Arts (3), Commerce (3), Electrical (2), Aerospace (2), Civil (2), Library Science (2), and BBA (1).

overview: Medical Officer Selection Board-2025 (MOSB-2025), Directorate General, Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force (ITBP), Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt. of India has released official advertisement for direct recruitment of Group 'A' Medical Officers in Central Armed Police Forces (BSF, CRPF, ITBP, SSB) & Assam Rifles.

A total of 282 Group 'A' vacancies are to be filled: Super Specialist Medical Officers (Second-in-Command) - 05 posts, Specialist Medical Officers (Deputy Commandant) - 162 posts, and Medical Officers (Assistant Commandant) - 115 posts (including 10% reservation for Ex-Servicemen).

faqs.question: Can GNM freshers apply for GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: No. GNM freshers without the required experience are not eligible for this recruitment. For candidates applying through the GNM qualification, the notification requires: GNM/Diploma in General Nursing Midwifery from a recognized institute, registration with State or Indian Nursing Council, AND 2 years of experience after acquiring the qualification in a minimum 50-bedded hospital. Candidates with B.Sc Nursing or B.Sc Nursing (Post Basic) can apply as freshers provided they have valid nursing registration.

faqs.question: Is work experience required for GNM candidates?
faqs.answer: Yes. GNM candidates must have 2 years of experience after acquiring the GNM qualification in a minimum 50-bedded hospital. The experience must be obtained after acquiring the qualification and supported by proper documentary proof. B.Sc Nursing candidates do not require hospital experience.

faqs.question: Can candidates registered with Nursing Councils outside Uttar Pradesh apply?
faqs.answer: Yes. Candidates registered with a State Nursing Council outside Uttar Pradesh or the Indian Nursing Council can apply, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements. However, regarding reservation, only permanent residents/domiciles of Uttar Pradesh are eligible for SC/ST/OBC/EWS reserved posts. Other-state candidates will be considered under the Unreserved (UR) category.

faqs.question: Are Chhattisgarh state students eligible for GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates from Chhattisgarh (and all other Indian states) can apply if they satisfy the prescribed eligibility conditions (B.Sc Nursing or GNM with 2 yrs experience + Registration + Age). However, Chhattisgarh domicile candidates cannot claim UP reservation benefits and will be treated as Unreserved (UR) candidates.

faqs.question: Why is the GIMS Staff Nurse notification/link not showing on the official website?
faqs.answer: The notification has been officially released. The advertisement (Advt. No. GIMS/2026/Manpower/NT-03/10) is dated 09 August 2026, and online applications started on 10 August 2026. The application window is open until 07 September 2026 for 100 Staff Nurse (Non-Teaching) posts on the official GIMS website www.gims.ac.in.

faqs.question: Why is the GIMS Staff Nurse vacancy not listed on Sarkari Result?
faqs.answer: A vacancy does not need to appear on Sarkari Result or third-party websites to be official. The official GIMS website (www.gims.ac.in) is the final authority. The notification has been released and online applications are active. Candidates should verify details directly from the official GIMS website.

faqs.question: Where can I get the direct application link for GIMS Staff Nurse?
faqs.answer: The online application is available through the official GIMS recruitment portal at www.gims.ac.in. Candidates should complete registration, fill details, upload photo/signature/documents, pay the fee, and submit the form online between 10 August 2026 and 07 September 2026.

faqs.question: Can you make a detailed video on the full notification once available?
faqs.answer: The notification is already available covering all 16 key points: 100 vacancies, B.Sc Nursing vs GNM eligibility, GNM 2-year 50-bed hospital experience, Nursing Council registration, age limit (21-40 yrs), category-wise reservation, UP domicile rules, application fee (UR/OBC ₹1298, SC/ST ₹944), CBT exam pattern (100 MCQs), syllabus, 0.25 negative marking, exam cities, and selection process.

faqs.question: What is the overall age limit for GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026?
faqs.answer: The general age limit is Minimum 21 years and Maximum 40 years as on 01 July 2026. Candidates must be at least 21 years old and not older than 40 years on the cutoff date, subject to category-wise age relaxations.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and relaxation for the OBC category?
faqs.answer: Eligible OBC candidates of Uttar Pradesh receive up to 5 years of age relaxation (maximum age 45 years). However, this relaxation applies strictly to permanent residents/domiciles of UP. OBC candidates from other states will be treated as Unreserved (UR) candidates and must fall within the 40-year limit.

faqs.question: Is the upper age limit 40 years?
faqs.answer: Yes, the general upper age limit is 40 years as on 1 July 2026. Age relaxations include: UP SC/ST/OBC (up to 5 years), UP Govt employees (up to 5 years), Persons with Disabilities (15 years), and Ex-Servicemen (up to 3 years after deducting service).

faqs.question: What is the complete GIMS Staff Nurse exam syllabus & pattern?
faqs.answer: The CBT consists of 100 MCQs for 100 marks (Duration: 2 hours). Section A (60 Questions) covers Core Nursing; Section B (25 Questions) covers Applied Sciences & Protocols; Section C (15 Questions) covers Basic Sciences, English, and Community Health. 80% questions test theoretical knowledge and 20% test practical knowledge. Negative marking is 0.25 mark per wrong answer. Qualifying marks: UR/EWS/OBC 40%, SC/ST 35%.

faqs.question: Where will the GIMS Staff Nurse exam centres be located?
faqs.answer: The CBT examination will be conducted in Delhi/NCR, Lucknow, Gorakhpur, and Varanasi. Candidates can indicate city preferences during application, though final allocation depends on slot availability as indicated on the Admit Card.

faqs.question: What is the GIMS Staff Nurse application/examination fee?
faqs.answer: The application fee (including 18% GST) is: UR / OBC / EWS: ₹1,298 (₹1100 + ₹198 GST); SC / ST (UP Domicile): ₹944 (₹800 + ₹144 GST); Divyang (PwD UP Domicile): Exempted (Nil). Fee is non-refundable.

faqs.question: Is a caste certificate essential to attach/upload?
faqs.answer: Yes, if claiming SC/ST/OBC/EWS reservation benefits. Only permanent residents/domiciles of Uttar Pradesh are eligible for reservation. OBC/EWS certificates must be issued on or after 01 April 2026. Candidates from other states claiming reserved categories will be treated as General/UR.

faqs.question: When will the CRPF Nursing application start?
faqs.answer: CRPF Nursing recruitment is completely separate from GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment. Candidates should not confuse GIMS with CRPF. GIMS Staff Nurse applications are open from 10 August to 07 September 2026 on www.gims.ac.in.

faqs.question: Where can we find full notification details for ESIC GNM?
faqs.answer: ESIC recruitment is separate from GIMS Staff Nurse recruitment. ESIC vacancies should be checked on www.esic.gov.in. Eligibility rules, hospital experience, and application dates vary between organizations.

faqs.question: Is anyone travelling to Delhi (NCR) for NORCET 11 preparation?
faqs.answer: NORCET 11 (conducted by AIIMS) and GIMS Staff Nurse 2026 are separate exams, though syllabus topics (Fundamentals, MS Nursing, Pediatrics, Obstetrics, Pharmacology) overlap significantly. Preparing for GIMS CBT also aids in NORCET preparation.

faqs.question: How are seats allocated across reserved vs general categories?
faqs.answer: Out of 100 total vacancies: UR: 40, OBC: 27, SC: 21, EWS: 10, ST: 2. Horizontal reservation applies for Women (20%), Ex-Servicemen (5%), PwD (4%), and DFF (2%). Non-UP candidates compete under 40 UR seats.

faqs.question: Is there any update on government hospital job openings vs private job options?
faqs.answer: GIMS Staff Nurse Recruitment 2026 is a permanent government sector recruitment for 100 regular Staff Nurse posts under UP Govt. B.Sc Nursing candidates and GNM candidates with 2 years 50-bed hospital experience are encouraged to apply before 07 September 2026.

faqs.question: Why are there 0 vacancies in Bihar, Jharkhand, Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Uttarakhand, etc. in SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: Because the 1,538 vacancies in this particular notification are backlog vacancies, not the new regular vacancies for the 2026–27 recruitment cycle. A backlog vacancy generally represents a reserved-category vacancy from an earlier recruitment that remained unfilled. Therefore, the distribution is completely different from what you would expect from a normal SBI Clerk notification. Zero in Delhi/Bihar/Haryana etc. does NOT mean SBI will have zero regular Clerk vacancies there this year.

faqs.question: Will SBI Clerk 2026 vacancies be updated or increased later?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but don't assume they will be. The current notification is specifically for the backlog drive. The much more important development for most aspirants will be the separate regular SBI Clerk notification, which should contain fresh state-wise vacancies for the new recruitment cycle. If your state has zero seats in the present notification, wait for the regular notification rather than concluding that SBI Clerk has no vacancy in your state.

faqs.question: Why is there no vacancy in Delhi, Haryana, and NCR for SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: This is a consequence of the backlog-vacancy nature of the current recruitment. It does not mean SBI has stopped recruiting Junior Associates in Delhi/NCR or Haryana. Also remember that SBI recruitment is organized according to State/UT/circle-wise vacancies, rather than simply according to where candidates live.

faqs.question: What should candidates from zero-vacancy states do for SBI Clerk 2026?
faqs.answer: Wait for the regular notification. If you're from Delhi, Haryana, Bihar, Jharkhand, Punjab, Uttarakhand, etc., choosing another state merely because it has backlog vacancies is not recommended unless you genuinely satisfy that state's local-language requirement and are eligible for the applicable reserved category. The regular notification is likely to be far more relevant.

faqs.question: Can I apply for SBI Clerk 2026 from another state?
faqs.answer: Yes, subject to the notification's conditions — but the important issue is the local language. SBI's Junior Associate recruitment is state/UT based. Candidates apply for vacancies of one State/UT only and must qualify the specified local-language test (LPT) where applicable. For example, living in Delhi does not prevent you from applying for Maharashtra, but if you select Maharashtra, you must be prepared for Marathi language requirements.

faqs.question: How strict is the Language Proficiency Test (LPT) in SBI Clerk recruitment?
faqs.answer: It is a mandatory qualifying requirement. The LPT checks whether you know the specified local language of the selected state (e.g., Marathi for Maharashtra, Gujarati for Gujarat, Tamil for Tamil Nadu, Odia for Odisha, Kannada for Karnataka, Malayalam for Kerala, Punjabi for Punjab, Bengali for West Bengal, Hindi/Urdu for UP). Candidates who cannot produce acceptable proof of having studied the specified local language in 10th or 12th standard must qualify the LPT. Failing the required LPT will result in disqualification.

faqs.question: Will applying outside your home state automatically cause LPT problems?
faqs.answer: No. Your home state is not the deciding factor. The important question is whether you can prove/meet the language requirement of the state applied for. A candidate from Delhi could apply for Maharashtra, but if they cannot establish Marathi proficiency through standard qualification routes, they may have to take the LPT. Do not choose a state simply because it has a lower cutoff.

faqs.question: If I apply for SBI Clerk from another state, where will my exam centre be?
faqs.answer: You can generally appear for the Preliminary and Mains examination at a notified examination centre of your choice/availability, subject to SBI's arrangements. However, your recruitment is against the state applied for. SBI's rules state that the local-language test (LPT) is conducted at a centre decided by SBI in the state applied for, at the candidate's own expense. (Exam centre ≠ state of recruitment).

faqs.question: How should candidates choose a state when applying for SBI Clerk?
faqs.answer: Choose the state where you genuinely satisfy the local-language requirement first; then compare vacancies and expected competition. The recommended sequence is: Language eligibility → vacancy → expected competition → posting preference. Remember that candidates are considered against the State/UT applied for and are posted in that state if selected.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Regular and Backlog vacancies in SBI recruitment?
faqs.answer: A Regular vacancy is a newly identified vacancy for the current recruitment cycle. A Backlog vacancy is a reserved vacancy from an earlier recruitment that remained unfilled and is carried forward to be filled through a special drive. The current 1,538-post notification is specifically a backlog recruitment, which explains the unusual state-wise vacancy distribution.

faqs.question: Can eligible candidates apply for both Regular and Backlog SBI Clerk recruitments?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you are eligible for both and SBI permits applications for both drives. They are separate recruitment drives. For example, an eligible SC/ST/OBC candidate could potentially participate in both the backlog recruitment and the upcoming regular recruitment, provided they satisfy the eligibility conditions of both.

faqs.question: Will the exams for SBI Clerk Regular and Backlog recruitments be separate?
faqs.answer: Do not assume they will be combined. The current notification is a separate Special Recruitment Drive, so candidates should treat it as a separate recruitment unless SBI subsequently announces otherwise. Expect separate application and exam processes.

faqs.question: Can General (Unreserved) candidates apply for these SBI Clerk backlog vacancies?
faqs.answer: No. The 1,538 backlog vacancies are reserved exclusively for SC, ST, and OBC candidates carried forward from previous recruitment drives. Unreserved / General category candidates cannot claim an SC/ST/OBC backlog seat.

faqs.question: What is the age limit and cutoff date for SBI Clerk Special Drive 2026?
faqs.answer: For the backlog notification, the basic age requirement is 20 to 28 years as of the cut-off date specified in the official notification, plus applicable relaxations for reserved categories (5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, up to 10–15 years for PwBD). Ensure you check your exact Date of Birth against the specific cut-off date stated in the notification.

faqs.question: Why are some states showing SC/ST vacancies but zero OBC vacancies?
faqs.answer: Because backlog vacancies are category-specific. If SBI had an SC/ST backlog in a particular state but no OBC backlog, it cannot convert or reassign those seats. A table showing SC: 0 | ST: 12 | OBC: 0 simply reflects historical unfilled reserved positions for that state, not a policy of ignoring OBC candidates.

faqs.question: Is the SBI Clerk 2026 question paper available in English?
faqs.answer: Yes. The examination paper is provided in English along with Hindi and the relevant regional language(s) depending on the state (e.g., English/Hindi/Marathi in Maharashtra, English/Hindi/Gujarati in Gujarat, English/Hindi/Odia in Odisha, English/Hindi/Bengali in WB, English/Hindi/Urdu in UP/Bihar). The question paper medium is separate from the LPT requirement.

faqs.question: Did SBI Apprentice recruitment reduce regular Clerk vacancies?
faqs.answer: No. There is no basis in the official notification to conclude that Apprentice recruitment reduced Clerk vacancies. SBI Apprentice and SBI Junior Associate are different recruitment streams. The 1,538-post announcement is a backlog drive, and the upcoming regular Junior Associate recruitment will provide the actual fresh vacancy numbers.

faqs.question: Why are videos claiming 9,000 to 11,000+ vacancies when this notification says 1,538?
faqs.answer: Because numbers like 9,000 or 11,000+ circulating online represent projected estimates for the upcoming Regular recruitment cycle, whereas 1,538 is the officially notified count for the Special Backlog Drive. Do not add backlog figures to unofficial YouTube estimates; wait for SBI's official regular notification.

faqs.question: Where can candidates download the official SBI Clerk notification PDF?
faqs.answer: The official notification should always be downloaded directly from SBI's official careers portal at sbi.bank.in/web/careers or bank.sbi/careers. Always verify the advertisement on SBI's official site rather than relying on unverified Telegram or social media files.

faqs.question: Should students run a Twitter/X campaign regarding uneven SBI Clerk vacancies?
faqs.answer: Campaigns will not force SBI to convert reserved backlog seats into UR seats, as backlog vacancies are legally reserved carried-forward positions. If raising concerns, the appropriate request to SBI would be to clarify state-wise vacancy requirements and release the regular SBI Clerk notification with fresh vacancies at the earliest.

education: 1. Gender Requirement: Only female candidates (केवल महिला अभ्यर्थी) are eligible to apply for Anganwadi Worker & Helper posts.
2. Minimum Educational Qualification: Intermediate (12th Class) pass or equivalent from a recognized board.
3. Maximum Educational Qualification: Post Graduation (PG). Merit score will be evaluated across Intermediate, Graduation, and PG qualifications.
4. Mandatory Local Residency: Candidate MUST be a permanent resident of the concerned Gram Sabha / Ward / Urban Area for which the vacancy is listed.
5. Special Preferences & Documents: Widow candidates must provide husband death certificate & family register document. Divorced or abandoned women must provide valid court decree.
6. Income Limits & Verification: Income certificate issued by Revenue Dept (Govt Order 3959/1-9-11-Raj-9 & 22/2015/2123/26-2-2015) must be verified online via e-District portal.
eligibility.ageLimit: As on 01 July 2026: Minimum 18 Years, Maximum 35 Years. Age will be verified strictly according to the date of birth recorded in the High School (10th) certificate.
medicalStandards: Candidate must be physically and mentally fit to perform field-level child care and Anganwadi center services.

salary.payLevel: Honorarium Based Appointment (मानदेय पर आधारित सीधी भर्ती)
salary.initialPay: Fixed Monthly Honorarium: Anganwadi Worker approx ₹7,500 - ₹9,000 / month; Anganwadi Helper approx ₹4,500 - ₹5,500 / month (including Central & State Government contributions).
allowances: Performance incentives, mobile allowance, special supplementary nutrition handling honorarium, and medical/insurance cover as applicable under UP Govt rules.

selectionProcess.description: Selection is purely merit-based calculated from percentage of marks obtained in Intermediate (12th) up to Post Graduation. Total percentage scored is divided by 10 (e.g., 45% = 4.5 points, 59% = 5.9 points). High school marks are used only for age verification and NOT included in merit.
Grading & CGPA systems are calculated to exact percentage and calculated up to 3 decimal places without rounding off.

Online verification of Residence (निवास), Income (आय), and Caste (जाति) certificates via e-District UP portal (edistrict.up.gov.in). Unverified caste/income certificates will result in treatment as Unreserved category or rejection under BPL quota.
Final Ward / Gram Sabha wise merit list will be uploaded on https://upanganwadibharti.in. No written exam or interview will be conducted.

howToApplySteps: Step 1: Visit the official portal of UP Anganwadi Bharti at https://upanganwadibharti.in.
Step 2: Select District 'Maharajganj' and choose your respective Bal Vikas Project (Partawal, Sadar, Nautanwa, etc.) and Ward / Gram Sabha.
Step 3: Complete registration with mobile number, Aadhaar details, personal information, income certificate number, caste certificate number, and educational marks (12th to PG).
Step 4: Upload scanned self-attested copies of photo, signature, High School certificate, 12th mark sheet, higher qualification certificates, and domicile certificate.
Step 5: Review all entered details carefully and submit the form online before 01 September 2026 Midnight (12:00 PM). Take a printout for future reference (no hard copy submission required).

overview: The Karnataka School Education Department (Department of Public Instruction), Government of Karnataka, has officially announced the mega recruitment drive for 15,000 teaching posts in Government Primary and High Schools for the 2026-27 academic session.

The recruitment notice was published on 12 August 2026, with district-wise gazette notices issued through the Karnataka Gazette (e-Rajyapatra) portal. howToApplySteps: Step 1: Register on the Government NAPS Portal (www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) as a candidate and generate a 10-digit NAPS Registration Number.

overview: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Aircraft Division, Nasik, a Maharatna Central Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, Govt. of India, has published official advertisement Advt. No. HAL/T&D/1614/2026/265 inviting online applications for 1-year apprenticeship training of 355 ITI Trade Apprentices for the year 2026 under the Apprentices Act, 1961.

The recruitment drive offers 355 ITI Apprentice posts across 17 trades including Fitter (110), COPA (70), Electrician (35), Turner (25), Machinist (22), Painter (10), Aerospace Structural Fitter (10), Carpenter (10), Sheet Metal Worker (10), Welder (10), Machinist Grinder (10), Electronics Mechanic (8), Motor Vehicle Mechanic (6), RAC Mechanic (6), Draughtsman Mechanical (5), Tool & Die Maker Jig & Fixture (4), and Tool & Die Maker Die & Mould (4).
Candidates who have passed 10th Class (SSC) and regular ITI (NCVT/SCVT) in the respective trade can register on NAPS portal and fill the online application form by 04th September 2026.

howToApplySteps: Step 1: Register on NAPS Portal (www.apprenticeshipindia.gov.in) with SSC (10th) & ITI details and generate 10-digit Registration Number starting with A0XXXXX.
Step 2: Ensure your NAPS profile is 100% completed with mandatory e-KYC, beneficiary ID, and Aadhaar seeded SBI savings bank account for DBT.
Step 3: Upload original scanned documents on NAPS profile (Aadhaar Card, SSC Marksheet, ITI Passing Certificate/Marksheets, Bank Passbook).
Step 4: Open HAL Nasik Online Application Form via link https://zfrmz.in/KSfP6So9GXJgaRx1NTv5 or scan QR Code given in notification.
Step 5: Fill all personal details, NAPS registration number, SSC marks, ITI trade marks, and category accurately as per official documents.
Step 6: Submit the online form. On successful submission, message 'Thank You ! Your Form is Submitted Successfully!' will be displayed.
Step 7: Take a printout of submitted form and keep safely for reference during physical document verification at HAL Nasik.

selectionProcess.description: 100 Objective MCQs (120 Minutes). overview: Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB / RSMSSB), Jaipur has released detailed advertisement Advt. No. 10/2026 for Junior Engineer Joint Direct Recruitment 2026 (कनिष्ठ अभियंता संयुक्त सीधी भर्ती-2026) for 874 vacancies across PWD, Water Resources Department, and PHED.

The recruitment drive invites online applications for 874 Junior Engineer posts carrying 7th Pay Commission Pay Matrix Level L-10 across Civil Degree (470 posts), Civil Diploma (372 posts), and Mechanical/Electrical Diploma (32 posts) cadres in Non-TSP (793) and TSP (81) areas.

Eligible candidates holding a B.E / B.Tech or Diploma in Civil, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering can submit online applications via Rajasthan SSO Portal (sso.rajasthan.gov.in) from 16th August 2026 until 14th September 2026 (11:59 PM).

selectionProcess.description: 120 MCQs (120 Marks - 2 Hours duration). Section A: Rajasthan General Knowledge (History, Art & Culture, Geography, Administrative System - 40 Marks). Section B: Engineering Branch Subject (80 Marks). 1/3rd negative marking for incorrect answers. Minimum qualifying marks: 40%.
Candidates must darken option 'E' if not attempting a question. If >10% of questions are left completely blank without option E, the candidate is disqualified.
Shortlisted candidates from the merit list report for document verification with original certificates.
Final allotment to PWD, WRD, or PHED conducted based on Merit-cum-Priority filled during online application.

howToApplySteps: Step 1: Visit Rajasthan SSO Portal at http://sso.rajasthan.gov.in and log in using your SSO ID and Password.
Step 2: Navigate to Citizen Apps (G2C) -> Select 'Recruitment Portal'.
Step 3: If OTR (One Time Registration) fee is not paid previously, complete OTR tab, select category, upload Aadhaar/JanAadhaar, and pay OTR fee (₹600 for UR; ₹400 for Reserved/PwD).
Step 4: Locate 'JUNIOR ENGINEER JOINT DIRECT RECRUITMENT 2026 (Advt No. 10/2026)' and click 'Apply Now'.
Step 5: Fill in post choice (Degree/Diploma), department priority (PWD, WRD, PHED), qualification details, and personal info.
Step 6: Fetch live photo via OTR webcam capture, check details in Preview, and click 'Final Submit'.
Step 7: Download and print out the submitted application form (containing Application ID) for future reference during document verification.

faqs.question: What is the last date to apply online for RSMSSB Junior Engineer (JEN) 2026?

faqs.question: What is the total number of vacancies in RSMSSB JEN Recruitment 2026?

faqs.answer: Yes! Candidates from all states can apply. Other state candidates will be considered under the Unreserved (General) category.

faqs.question: Are final year degree/diploma students eligible for RSMSSB JEN 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes! Final year appearing candidates can apply, provided they acquire the educational qualification by the date of the written examination.

faqs.question: What is the exam pattern and marking scheme for RSMSSB JEN 2026?
faqs.answer: 120 MCQs (120 Marks, 2 Hours): 40 Marks for Rajasthan GK and 80 Marks for Engineering subject. 1/3rd negative marking applies. Minimum 40% marks required to pass.

faqs.question: Is option 'E' mandatory in OTR / OMR exam?
faqs.answer: Yes! Candidates must darken option 'E' for any unattempted question. Failing to fill option E for more than 10% of questions results in disqualification.

faqs.answer: The written examination is tentatively scheduled to be conducted in February 2027.

overview: The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), Ministry of Railways, Government of India, have issued the official Detailed Centralised Employment Notice (CEN No. 04/2026) for direct recruitment to 3,993 vacancies of Junior Engineer (JE) across Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Signal & Telecommunication (S&T), and Track Machine departments, as well as Depot Material Superintendent (DMS) in the Stores Department.

This recruitment provides a premier career opportunity for Diploma holders and Engineering Graduates (B.E. / B.Tech / B.Sc Engg) across all major engineering disciplines. Selected candidates will be appointed in Pay Level 6 of the 7th Central Pay Commission (7th CPC) Pay Matrix, with a starting Basic Pay of ₹35,400/- per month along with Dearness Allowance (DA), House Rent Allowance (HRA), Transport Allowance, and comprehensive Railway Medical benefits.

The selection process is conducted through a multi-tier assessment comprising 1st Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-I - Screening), 2nd Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-II - Core Technical & General Abilities), Document Verification (DV shortlisted at 1:1 ratio based on CBT-II merit), and Standard Medical Examination (ME). For CBT-II, candidates are mapped into 4 distinct Exam Groups: Civil & Allied Engineering, Electrical & Allied Engineering, Electronics & Allied Engineering, and Mechanical & Allied Engineering.

Eligible candidates holding a 3-Year Diploma in Engineering or B.E. / B.Tech / B.Sc Engg degree in relevant engineering fields, aged between 18 to 33 years as on 01.01.2027, can submit their application online through the unified RRB portal at www.rrbapply.gov.in between 14th August 2026 and 13th September 2026 (23:59 Hours). Candidates must choose only ONE RRB and indicate their order of preference for Railway Zones/Units and notified posts within that RRB.

education: CATEGORY 1: Junior Engineer / Civil (Posts: P.Way, Works, Bridge, Design Drawing & Estimation, Track Machine, Research Civil):

• Three (3) years Diploma in Civil Engineering OR B.Sc. in Civil Engineering of three years duration OR Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (B.E. / B.Tech) in Civil Engineering or combination of any sub-stream of basic streams of Civil Engineering from a recognized University / Institute.
CATEGORY 2: Junior Engineer / Mechanical (Posts: Carriage & Wagon, Diesel Mechanical, Workshop, Design Mechanical, Millwright, Track Machine):

• Three (3) years Diploma in Mechanical / Production / Automobile / Electrical / Electronics / Manufacturing / Mechatronics / Industrial / Machining / Instrumentation & Control / Tools & Machining / Tools & Die Making Engineering OR B.E. / B.Tech in relevant engineering branches from a recognized University / Institute.
CATEGORY 3: Junior Engineer / Electrical (Posts: General Services, TRD, TRS, EMU, Workshop, Design Drawing & Estimation):

• Three (3) years Diploma in Mechanical / Electrical / Electronics Engineering OR combination of any sub-stream of basic streams of Mechanical / Electrical / Electronics Engineering OR B.E. / B.Tech in relevant engineering streams from a recognized University / Institute.
CATEGORY 4: Junior Engineer / Signal & Telecommunication (Posts: Signal, Telecommunication, Workshop, Design):

• Three (3) years Diploma in Electrical / Electronics / Information Technology / Communication Engineering / Computer Science & Engineering / Computer Science / Computer Engineering OR combination of sub-streams OR B.E. / B.Tech in relevant branch from a recognized University / Institute.
CATEGORY 5: Depot Material Superintendent (DMS - Stores Department):
• Three (3) years Diploma in Engineering in ANY discipline OR B.E. / B.Tech in ANY engineering stream from a recognized University / Institution.
CRUCIAL QUALIFICATION CLAUSES:
• Candidates must possess the prescribed qualification on or before the closing date of application (13.09.2026). Candidates awaiting results of final examination are NOT eligible.

medicalStandards: MEDICAL FITNESS & VISUAL ACUITY STANDARDS (IRMM Vol-I Chapter 5):

• Medical Standard A-3: Physically fit in all respects. Distance Vision: 6/9, 6/9 with or without glasses (power of lenses not to exceed 2D). Near Vision: Sn: 0.6, 0.6 with or without glasses. Must pass tests for Colour Vision, Binocular Vision, Night Vision, and Mesopic Vision. (CRITICAL: Candidates with LASIK surgery or surgical correction are NOT eligible for A-3 posts).

• Medical Standard B-1: Physically fit in all respects. Distance Vision: 6/9, 6/12 with or without glasses (power of lenses not to exceed 4D). Near Vision: Sn: 0.6, 0.6 with or without glasses when reading/close work required. Must pass Colour, Binocular, Night, and Mesopic vision tests. (LASIK surgery eligible only if surgery completed >= 1 year ago with specialist certificate, residual corneal thickness >= 425 microns on Pachymetry, normal fundus, and no progressive eye disease).

• Medical Standard B-2: Physically fit in all respects. Distance Vision: 6/9, 6/12 with or without glasses (power of lenses not to exceed 4D). Near Vision: Sn: 0.6, 0.6 with or without glasses when reading/close work required.
• Medical Standard C-1: Physically fit in all respects. Distance Vision: 6/12, 6/18 with or without glasses. Near Vision: Sn: 0.6, 0.6 with or without glasses when reading/close work required.
• Failure in Medical Standard: Candidates failing to meet the medical fitness standard of their opted post will not be empanelled and NO alternate appointment will be offered by Railways.

selectionProcess.stage: Stage I: 1st Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-I) - Screening Test
selectionProcess.description: Qualifying screening examination of 90 minutes duration (120 minutes for eligible scribe candidates) consisting of 100 objective MCQs carrying 100 marks: Mathematics (30 Qs / 30 Marks), General Intelligence & Reasoning (25 Qs / 25 Marks), General Awareness (15 Qs / 15 Marks), and General Science (30 Qs / 30 Marks). Negative marking of 1/3rd mark applies for every wrong answer. Normalized scores will be used solely to shortlist candidates for CBT-II at 15 times the community-wise vacancy of the chosen RRB. Minimum qualifying marks: UR 40%, EWS 40%, OBC-NCL 30%, SC 30%, ST 25% (2 marks relaxation for PwBD).

selectionProcess.stage: Stage II: 2nd Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-II) - Core Technical & General Abilities
selectionProcess.description: Rank-determining examination of 120 minutes duration (160 minutes for eligible scribe candidates) comprising 150 objective MCQs carrying 150 marks: General Awareness (15 Qs / 15 Marks), Physics & Chemistry (15 Qs / 15 Marks), Basics of Computers and Applications (10 Qs / 10 Marks), Basics of Environment and Pollution Control (10 Qs / 10 Marks), and Technical Abilities of the chosen Exam Group (100 Qs / 100 Marks). Negative marking of 1/3rd mark applies. A Virtual Calculator will be made available on the computer monitor during CBT-II. Minimum qualifying marks: UR 40%, EWS 40%, OBC 30%, SC 30%, ST 25%.

selectionProcess.stage: Stage III: Normalisation & Calculation of Merit Index
selectionProcess.description: To generate a common merit list of candidates across different Exam Groups eligible for common posts, a Merit Index is computed using the official formula: Merit Index = Sq + (St - Sq) * [(M - Mq) / (Mt - Mq)], where Sq=350 (score assigned to Mq), St=900 (score assigned to Mt), Mq=40 (qualifying marks for UR), and Mt=Mean marks of top 0.1% or top 10 candidates. The allotment of posts/zones is done strictly on the basis of this Merit Index.

Shortlisting for DV is done RRB-wise at the rate of 1:1 of the notified vacancies based on CBT-II merit and post preferences. Candidates must produce all original educational certificates, caste/community certificates, NOC, and upload scanned color copies of Photo & Signature on the portal https://oirms-ir.gov.in/rrbdv prior to the DV date.

Shortlisted candidates undergo rigorous medical fitness evaluation conducted by Railway Medical Authorities to ascertain physical fitness and visual acuity under medical standards A-3, B-1, B-2, or C-1 as prescribed for the allotted post.

syllabus.section: 7. Technical Abilities: Civil & Allied Engineering Exam Group (Annexure VIII-A)
topics: Engineering Mechanics: Forces, Moments, Equilibrium, Friction, Centroid, Center of Gravity, Simple Machines
Building Construction & Materials: Substructure, Superstructure, Masonry, Bricks, Stones, Timber, Plastics, Bitumen, PVC, CPVC
Construction Techniques: Earthwork, Foundations, Dewatering, Cofferdams, Scaffolding, Shoring, Cavity walls, Doors/Windows
Building Maintenance & Finishes: Plastering, Pointing, Painting, Flooring, Roofing, Cracks repairs (Grouting, Guniting, Epoxy)
Building Drawing & CAD Software: Conventions, Lines, Symbols, Municipal Byelaws, AutoCAD, Auto Civil, 3D Max, Plan/Elevation/Section

Surveying: Chain, Compass, Leveling (Auto/Tilting level), Contouring, Theodolite, Tacheometry, Curves, Total Station, Aerial Survey & Remote Sensing
Geotechnical Engineering & Soil Mechanics: Soil physical properties, Permeability, Seepage, Shear strength, Bearing capacity, Compaction, Soil stabilization
Hydraulics & Irrigation: Fluid properties, Hydrostatic pressure, Pipe flow, Open channels, Hydraulic machines, Hydrology, Reservoirs, Percolation tanks, Diversion works
Mechanics & Theory of Structures: Stress-Strain, SFD/BMD, Moment of Inertia, Trusses, Direct/Bending stresses, Slope-Deflection, Columns, Continuous beams
Design of Concrete Structures: Working Stress & Limit State methods, Singly/Doubly reinforced sections, Shear & Bond, T-Beams, Slabs, Columns, Footings
Design of Steel Structures: IS Codes, Connections, Tension/Compression members, Steel roof trusses, Beams, Column bases

Transportation Engineering: Railway Engineering (Gauges, Permanent Way, Track geometrics, Points & Crossings, Maintenance), Bridges (Site selection, Inspection, Abutments, Piers), Tunnels (Excavation, Strata, Lining, Ventilation)
Highway & Environmental Engineering: Geometric design, Pavements, Traffic engineering, Drainage, Water supply engineering, Domestic sewage, Plumbing

syllabus.section: 8. Technical Abilities: Electrical & Allied Engineering Exam Group (Annexure VIII-B)
topics: Basic Concepts: Resistance, Inductance, Capacitance, Voltage, Current, Power, Energy and their units
Circuit Law & Theorems: Kirchhoff's Laws (KCL/KVL), Network theorems, Thevenin, Norton, Superposition, Maximum Power Transfer
Magnetic Circuits: Flux, MMF, Reluctance, Magnetic materials, Electromagnetic induction, Self & Mutual inductance
AC Fundamentals: Peak, RMS, Average values, Sinusoidal waveforms, Series/Parallel R-L-C circuits, Resonance, 3-Phase Star/Delta connections
Measurement & Instruments: 1-Phase & 3-Phase power measurement (2-Wattmeter method), Ammeters, Voltmeters, Wattmeters, Megger, AC Bridges, CRO, CT, PT, Earth Fault detection

Electrical Machines: DC Motors & Generators (Construction, Principles, Characteristics, Speed control, Starters, Losses/Efficiency), Transformers (1-Phase & 3-Phase, O.C./S.C. tests, Parallel operation, Auto-transformers), 3-Phase Induction Motors (RMF, Torque-Speed curves, Starters), Fractional KW & Single Phase Motors
Synchronous Machines: 3-Phase EMF generation, Armature reaction, Voltage regulation, Parallel operation of alternators, Synchronizing, Synchronous motors

Generation, Transmission & Distribution: Power station types, Load factor, Diversity factor, Tariffs, Fault analysis, Switchgear & Protection (Circuit breakers, HRC fuses, Buchholz relay, Merz-Price protection, Lightning arresters, Cable ratings/derating)
Estimation & Costing: Lighting schemes, Industrial wiring installation, Indian Electricity (IE) Rules, Earthing practices
Utilization of Electrical Energy: Illumination principles, Electric heating, Electric welding, Electroplating, Electric traction drives and motors
Basic Electronics: PN Junction Diodes, Zener Diodes, BJT (NPN/PNP), JFET, Rectifiers, Inverters, Simple amplifier circuits
